slides.title: What is a Set?
slides.text:
Before we start, remember: A Set is just a collection of distinct objects.

Imagine a basket. Anything we put inside that basket is a 'member' of the set.

slides.title: 1. Finite Sets
slides.text:
A Finite Set is a set where we can count the members, and the counting comes to an end.

Example: A set of vowels. We count: a, e, i, o, u. Stop. There are no more.

slides.title: Cardinal Number
slides.text:
Because a Finite set ends, it has a specific number of members.

We call this the Cardinal Number, written as n(A).
Here, n(A) = 5.

slides.title: 2. Infinite Sets
slides.text:
An Infinite Set is different. It never ends.

Imagine counting all the numbers: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5... You could go on forever and never finish!

slides.title: The Ellipsis (...)
slides.text:
Since we can't write all the numbers, we use three dots called an Ellipsis.

{ 1, 2, 3, ... }

This symbol tells us the set continues forever.

slides.title: Summary
slides.text:
• Finite: Has an end. We can find n(A).
  • Infinite: Goes on forever. We use '...'

Next, we will try a quiz to see if you can spot the difference!
